text: Thermal fatigue: There was no evidence of any additional microcracking that could be attributed to thermal cycling (3 min at LN2 followed by 15 min at RT); In general, the SBS at LN2 temperature was not affected much by the thermal cycling (with the exception of laminates 1ATC and 2ACC), although uni- tape layup A showed better performance compared to layup B for most of the comparisons; There was no difference in failure behavior either because of thermal cycling prior to static testing • Mechanical fatigue: VACNT reinforced laminate A experienced runout (> 12,000 cycles) @ 40% of shear strength Page 23 of 30 Approved for Public Release (a) (b) Figure 25. SBS Strength and Acoustic Emission onset for (a) unitape and (b) fabric laminates Tensile Testing, ASTM D3039 • Static Testing o Laminates made with layup A outperformed laminates made with layup B in strength and damage onset at cryogenic conditions o Most specimens exhibited valid failure modes and expected test and fracture behaviors. However, grip slippage proved problematic during cryogenic tests and some specimens displayed tab delamination failures or failure close to the tab ends Page 24 of 30 Approved for Public Release o Post-failure crack analysis: Mixed results regarding crack spacing measurements were obtained depending upon layup, reinforcement and test temperature, and no specific trends could be established o Incremental loading of laminates made with layup A: Testing showed that load-drops observed earlier during cryogenic testing were the artifacts of tab bond-line damage and did not affect the ultimate strength measured on these specimens; Transverse cracks were terminated in the interlaminar region between the +-45° plies so no cracks travelled into the outer 45° ply. • Thermal fatigue: There was no evidence of any additional microcracking that could be attributed to thermal cycling (3 min at LN2 followed by 15 min at RT); Small differences were noted in residual strength following 200 cycles; Layup A showed slightly better performance compared to layup B; There was no difference in failure behavior either because of thermal cycling prior to static testing Fabric laminates Short Beam Shear (SBS) Testing, ASTM D2344 • Static Testing o Laminates made with layup A showed an improvement in onset of AE activity when tested at both RT and cryogenic conditions. Also, addition of CNTs did not impact shear strength at RT, while some decrease was observed under LN2 testing. On the other hand, laminates made with layup B resulted in decrease in stress level for onset of AE activity, and the shear strength was also negatively impacted by CNTs at RT and cryogenic testing. o In both laminate layups (layup A: [0/45/-45/90] and layup B: [45/90/-45/0] ), delamination 2s 2s was observed at multiple ply interfaces for baseline laminates tested at RT and at LN2, whereas for VACNTs interleaved laminates, a dominant single crack was observed at the mid- plane for majority of the laminates tested • Thermal fatigue: The SBS at LN2 temperature for VACNT interleaved laminates was not affected much by the thermal cycling conducted here; There was no difference in failure behavior either
